Here's the U.S. core inflation rate (Core CPI year-over-year) from January 2015 to December 2016:

| Month | Core Inflation Rate |
|-------|-------------------|
| Jan 2015 | 1.6% |
| Feb 2015 | 1.7% |
| Mar 2015 | 1.8% |
| Apr 2015 | 1.8% |
| May 2015 | 1.8% |
| Jun 2015 | 1.8% |
| Jul 2015 | 1.8% |
| Aug 2015 | 1.8% |
| Sep 2015 | 1.9% |
| Oct 2015 | 1.9% |
| Nov 2015 | 2.0% |
| Dec 2015 | 2.1% |
| Jan 2016 | 2.2% |
| Feb 2016 | 2.3% |
| Mar 2016 | 2.2% |
| Apr 2016 | 2.1% |
| May 2016 | 2.2% |
| Jun 2016 | 2.2% |
| Jul 2016 | 2.2% |
| Aug 2016 | 2.3% |
| Sep 2016 | 2.2% |
| Oct 2016 | 2.1% |
| Nov 2016 | 2.1% |
| Dec 2016 | 2.2% |

**Key observations:**
- Core inflation gradually increased from 1.6% in January 2015 to around 2.2% by late 2016
- The rate remained relatively stable throughout most of 2015 in the 1.8% range
- 2016 saw core inflation consistently above 2.0%, closer to the Federal Reserve's target
- This period reflected the economy's continued recovery from the Great Recession

*Note: Core CPI excludes volatile food and energy prices and is measured as year-over-year percentage change.*
